notes: Draft. Unit Check pre and post forms for Lists, Numbers and Talk. All content is invented or generic. Form A is taken before the unit with no technique required; Form B after. Keep the forms out of practice draws. The scores mean "your score on Mnemos tasks", never proof that the method works: some change is simply learning the task. Do not show Form B as a prize.

checks.title: Unit Check: Lists
checks.when: Form A in the first week of the unit (Week 3), Form B in the last (Week 6).

instructions.A: Use your own way. Study the list and the steps for the time shown, then write them back in order.
instructions.B: Use any method you like. Study the list and the steps for the time shown, then write them back in order.

steps.text: Fold a sheet of card in half.
Press the fold flat with a ruler.
Draw a big cake on the front.
Colour the cake pink with a crayon.
Glue a gold star in the corner.
Write a short message inside with a pen.
Slide the card into an envelope.
Tie a ribbon around the envelope.
Fold a sheet of paper in half.
Press the fold flat with a book.
Draw ten short lines along the fold.
Cut along each line with scissors.
Open the sheet and curl it into a tube.
Glue the two short edges together.
Tape a thin strip of card on top as a handle.
Stick a gold star on the side.
Hang it on a hook by the window.

checks.difficultyNote: Both forms: 12 groceries and a 9-step procedure. Same aisle mix (3 fruit and vegetables, 2 dairy, 1 bakery, 2 meat and fish, 2 pantry, 1 drink, 1 household). Average item length: A 7.25 letters, B 7.08. Procedure step length: A 6.67 words, B 7.56. Each list has no two items that sound alike. The 9 procedure steps in both forms are everyday paper crafts with concrete keys. Parallel difficulty is by design and has not been tested on players; Form B only means "after", and some of any gain is learning the task.

checks.title: Unit Check: Numbers
checks.when: Form A in Week 14, Form B in Week 21.

instructions.A: Use your own way. Study the numbers for the time shown, then write them back.
instructions.B: Use any method you like, such as the Major System. Study the numbers for the time shown, then write them back.

checks.difficultyNote: Both forms use a fixed 12-digit number and a phone-shaped 10-digit number grouped 3-3-4. Rules each number passes: no repeated neighbouring digit, no run of three digits stepping the same way (such as 135 or 321), no pair of digits used twice, a first digit that is not zero for the 12-digit number, no emergency or year-like groups. 12-digit forms: A has {"distinct":9,"highDigits":6,"meanStep":4.18}, B has {"distinct":9,"highDigits":6,"meanStep":4.09}. Phone-shaped forms: A has {"distinct":7,"highDigits":5,"meanStep":4}, B has {"distinct":7,"highDigits":5,"meanStep":3.67}. The first digit of each of the first two phone groups is 0 or 1, which valid North American numbers cannot start with, so these cannot be a real number there. They are random digits for practice and not meant as real phone numbers. The reserve list holds six more 12-digit numbers that pass the same rules, for any later re-take.

checks.title: Unit Check: Talk
checks.when: Form A in Week 28, Form B in Week 30.

instructions.A: Use your own way. Study the seven points for the time shown, then write them back in order.
instructions.B: Use any method you like. Study the seven points for the time shown, then write them back in order.

points.text: Open by holding up a trowel.
Name the empty lot behind the school.
Show a drawing of eight raised beds.
Say which vegetables will grow there.
Describe the water barrel by the fence.
Explain the weekly work rota pinned to the gate.
Ask the volunteers to raise a hand.
Open by holding up a paperback.
Name the empty corner of the hallway.
Show a drawing of eight wooden shelves.
Say which comics and novels are welcome.
Describe the donation box by the door.
Explain the weekly tidy rota pinned to the board.
Ask the volunteers to sign a sheet.

checks.difficultyNote: Both forms are a seven-point plan for a small community project with the same shape (open with an object, name a place, show a drawing, say what is included, describe a container, explain a rota, ask for volunteers). Average point length: A 7 words, B 7.14. Keys are concrete nouns of similar length. Equal difficulty is by design, not tested on players.
